features.name: Mystic Arcanum (9th Level)
features.description: Choose one level 9 Warlock spell as an arcanum. You can cast it once without a spell slot, regaining that use on a Short Rest or a Long Rest, and you can replace the chosen spell when you gain a Warlock level.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.description: As a Magic action, you can regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.description: When you reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points, or an enemy within 10 feet of you drops to 0 Hit Points, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Fiend Spells
description: The following spells are always prepared for you and don't count against your prepared total, each becoming available at the Warlock level shown.
**Level 3.** Burning Hands, Command, Scorching Ray, Suggestion
**Level 5.** Fireball, Stinking Cloud
**Level 7.** Fire Shield, Wall of Fire
**Level 9.** Geas, Insect Plague

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.description: When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can add 1d10 to the roll. You can do this after the roll but before its effects apply. You can use this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest or a Long Rest, choose one damage type other than Force. You have Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. It vanishes and hurtles through a nightmare landscape until the end of your next turn, when it returns to its space or the nearest unoccupied space.
If the target isn't a Fiend, it takes 8d10 Psychic damage when it returns.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a level 5 or higher spell slot to use it again.

features.name: Archfey Spells
description: The following spells are always prepared for you and don't count against your prepared total, each becoming available at the Warlock level shown.
**Level 3.** Calm Emotions, Faerie Fire, Misty Step, Phantasmal Force, Sleep
**Level 5.** Blink, Plant Growth
**Level 7.** Dominate Beast, Greater Invisibility
**Level 9.** Dominate Person, Seeming

features.name: Steps of the Fey
description: You can cast Misty Step without expending a spell slot, drawing on a pool of free castings equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you cast Misty Step this way, choose one of the following effects: Refreshing Step grants you, or another creature you can see within 10 feet of your destination, 1d10 Temporary Hit Points; Taunting Step forces creatures within 5 feet of the space you left to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have Disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone but you until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Misty Escape
description: When you take damage, you can cast Misty Step as a Reaction, without spending a Pact Magic spell slot or a use of Steps of the Fey.

Two more effects join the choices available when you teleport with Steps of the Fey: Disappearing Step turns you Invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell, whichever comes first; Dreadful Step forces creatures within 5 feet of the space you left or the space you arrive in (your choice) to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or take 2d10 Psychic damage.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
description: You can't be Charmed.

When an attack roll hits you, you can take a Reaction to halve the damage you're about to take (rounded down) and force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker takes Psychic damage equal to the damage you took.
Once you use this Reaction, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot to restore your use of it.

features.name: Bewitching Magic
features.description: Immediately after you cast an Enchantment or Illusion spell using a spell slot, you can also cast Misty Step as part of the same action, without expending an additional spell slot.

features.name: Celestial Spells
description: The following spells are always prepared for you and don't count against your prepared total, each becoming available at the Warlock level shown.
**Level 3.** Aid, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, Lesser Restoration, Light, Sacred Flame
**Level 5.** Daylight, Revivify
**Level 7.** Guardian of Faith, Wall of Fire
**Level 9.** Greater Restoration, Summon Celestial

features.name: Healing Light
features.description: You gain a pool of d6s for channeling healing power, containing a number of dice equal to 1 plus your Warlock level. As a Bonus Action, you can spend dice from the pool, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die), rolling them and restoring that many Hit Points to yourself or to one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The pool refills completely when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Radiant Soul
features.description: You have Resistance to Radiant damage. In addition, once per turn when a spell you cast deals Radiant or Fire damage, you can add your Charisma modifier to that damage against one target of the spell.

features.name: Celestial Resilience
features.description: Whenever you use your Magical Cunning feature or finish a Short or Long Rest, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level plus your Charisma modifier. At the same time, you can choose up to five creatures you can see; each of them gains Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Warlock level (rounded down) plus your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Searing Vengeance
description: When you or an ally within 60 feet of you is about to make a Death Saving Throw, you can flare with radiant power to intervene. The dying creature regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum and can immediately end the Prone condition on itself.
Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of that creature take Radiant damage equal to 2d8 plus your Charisma modifier and have the Blinded condition until the end of the current turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Great Old One Spells
description: The following spells are always prepared for you and don't count against your prepared total, each becoming available at the Warlock level shown.
**Level 3.** Detect Thoughts, Dissonant Whispers, Phantasmal Force, Tasha's Hideous Laughter
**Level 5.** Clairvoyance, Hunger of Hadar
**Level 7.** Confusion, Summon Aberration
**Level 9.** Modify Memory, Telekinesis

features.name: Awakened Mind
description: As a Bonus Action, you can open a telepathic link with one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You and that creature can communicate telepathically for a number of minutes equal to your Warlock level, and the link keeps working as you move apart, up to a number of miles between you equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 mile).
You can also change the damage type of any damaging Warlock spell you cast to Psychic, and you can cast your Enchantment and Illusion Warlock spells without Verbal or Somatic components.

features.name: Clairvoyant Combatant
features.description: When you form a telepathic bond with a creature using Awakened Mind, you can force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you and you have Advantage on attack rolls against it for as long as the bond lasts. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot to restore your use of it.

features.name: Eldritch Hex
description: You always have the Hex spell prepared. When you cast it, the target also has Disadvantage on saving throws using the ability score you chose, for as long as the spell lasts.

You also gain Resistance to Psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals Psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of Psychic damage in return. In addition, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or any other means unless you allow it.

features.name: Create Thrall
description: When you cast Summon Aberration, you can choose to cast it without Concentration; if you do, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute.

The summoned aberration has Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level plus your Charisma modifier. The first time each turn it hits a creature affected by your Hex spell, it deals extra Psychic damage to that creature equal to Hex's bonus damage.

features.name: Spellcasting
description: You cast Wizard spells using Intelligence, and you can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus. You know three cantrips from the Wizard spell list and learn more as you gain levels.
You keep a spellbook that starts with six level 1 Wizard spells, and you add two Wizard spells to it whenever you gain a Wizard level. You can also copy other Wizard spells you find into it.
You prepare your spells from the spellbook, with the number set by your level, and you can change the list when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Ritual Adept
features.description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and is in your spellbook. You don't need to have the spell prepared.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.description: Once per day when you finish a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to half your Wizard level (rounded up). None of the recovered slots can be level 6 or higher.

features.name: Scholar
features.description: Choose one of the following skills you are proficient in: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You gain Expertise in that skill.

features.name: Wizard Subclass
features.description: You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Memorize Spell
features.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can swap one prepared Wizard spell for a different spell from your spellbook.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.description: Choose one level 1 and one level 2 spell in your spellbook, each with a casting time of an action. You can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. You can change the chosen spells when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

features.name: Signature Spells
features.description: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as signature spells. They are always prepared and don't count against your prepared total, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot, regaining that ability when you finish a Short Rest or a Long Rest.

features.name: Evocation Savant
description: Whenever you gain access to a new level of Wizard spell slots, you can add two Evocation spells of that level to your spellbook for free.
In addition, the time and gold you spend to copy an Evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against a cantrip of yours, the creature still takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from it.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: When you cast a Wizard Evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a success.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: Whenever you cast a Wizard Evocation spell, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

features.name: Overchannel
description: When you cast a Wizard spell of levels 1 through 5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with it.

The first time you do this after a Long Rest, there is no cost. Each later use before you finish a Long Rest deals 2d12 Necrotic damage to you per level of the spell, and this damage ignores Resistance and Immunity and increases by 1d12 per spell level each additional time.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
description: Whenever you gain access to a new level of Wizard spell slots, you can add two Abjuration spells of that level to your spellbook for free.
In addition, the time and gold you spend to copy an Abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
description: When you cast an Abjuration spell using a spell slot, you can weave a strand of its magic into a protective ward around yourself that lasts until you finish a Long Rest. The ward's hit points equal twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, after any Resistance or Vulnerability of yours is applied, the ward absorbs that damage in your place, and only damage exceeding its remaining hit points reaches you.
Casting another Abjuration spell with a spell slot restores hit points to the ward equal to twice the level of the slot spent, even if the ward has already dropped to 0.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.description: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your Reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage in the creature's place. If this reduces the ward to 0 hit points, the creature takes whatever damage remains.

features.name: Spell Breaker
description: You always have Counterspell and Dispel Magic prepared, and neither counts against the number of spells you have prepared. You can cast Dispel Magic as a Bonus Action, and you add your Proficiency Bonus to the ability check it calls for.
Whenever you cast either spell using a spell slot and it fails to counter or dispel its target, the slot is not expended.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.description: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have Resistance to damage dealt by spells.

features.name: Divination Savant
description: Whenever you gain access to a new level of Wizard spell slots, you can add two Divination spells of that level to your spellbook for free.
In addition, the time and gold you spend to copy a Divination spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Portent
features.description: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, roll two d20s and record the results; you keep them until you finish your next Long Rest. Before any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check is made by you or a creature you can see, you can spend one of these recorded numbers in place of the roll, doing so no more than once per turn. Each number is used up once spent.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.description: When you cast a Divination spell of level 2 or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The regained slot must be a lower level than the spell you cast and can be no higher than level 5.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you gain one benefit of your choice: Darkvision out to 120 feet (or an increase of 120 feet if you already have Darkvision), the ability to see invisible creatures and objects as though under the effect of the See Invisibility spell, or the ability to read and understand any language you can see written down. The benefit lasts until you finish a Short or Long Rest, and once you've used this feature you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Greater Portent
features.description: You now roll three d20s for your Portent feature instead of two.

features.name: Illusion Savant
description: Whenever you gain access to a new level of Wizard spell slots, you can add two Illusion spells of that level to your spellbook for free.
In addition, the time and gold you spend to copy an Illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Improved Illusions
description: You can cast Illusion spells without providing their Verbal components, and any Illusion spell you cast with a range of 10 feet or more has its range increased by 60 feet.

You always have the Minor Illusion cantrip prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know. You can cast it as a Bonus Action, and when you do, a single casting can create both a sound and an image.

features.name: Phantasmal Creatures
description: You always have the Summon Beast and Summon Fey spells prepared, and neither counts against the number of spells you have prepared. You can cast either spell as an Illusion spell instead of its normal school; the creature it summons appears spectral and translucent but otherwise functions normally.

You can cast Summon Beast or Summon Fey in this way once without expending a spell slot, though the summoned creature has only half its normal hit point maximum. Once you've done this with a given spell, you can't do so again with that spell until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of level 2 or higher to restore your use of it.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.description: When a creature hits you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between you and the attacker, causing the attack to miss you instead; the duplicate then disappears. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of level 2 or higher, requiring no action, to restore your use of it.

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.description: When you cast an Illusion spell of level 1 or higher using a spell slot, you can use a Bonus Action to make one inanimate, nonmagical object that's part of the illusion physically real. The object remains real for 1 minute or until the spell ends, whichever comes first, and it can't deal damage, impose conditions, or otherwise directly harm anyone.
